## Ownership & Lifetime
<a id="ownership-lifetime"></a>

### ❌ Circular std::shared_ptr reference causing memory leak

**Symptom:**
```cpp
class A { std::shared_ptr<B> b; }; class B { std::shared_ptr<A> a; };
```

**Risk:** Permanent memory leak from circular ownership

**Recommended Action:** Use std::weak_ptr for observer references that don't need ownership.


*Tags: shared_ptr, weak_ptr, ownership, memory leak, circular reference*

---

### ❌ Unnecessary replacement of raw pointers at C API boundaries

**Symptom:**
```cpp
Replace all raw pointers from C API with std::unique_ptr.
```

**Risk:** Breaking C API contracts and introducing ownership transfer bugs

**Recommended Action:** Keep raw pointers at C API boundaries but explicitly document ownership semantics. Use smart pointers only if you clearly control the entire lifecycle.


*Tags: raw pointer, c api, ownership, boundary*

---

### ❌ Attempting to move from const objects

**Symptom:**
```cpp
const std::unique_ptr<Foo> p; auto q = std::move(p);
```

**Risk:** Compilation failure, or unexpected copy instead of move

**Recommended Action:** Remove const from objects you need to transfer ownership from. const prevents move operations because they modify the source object.


*Tags: std::move, const, ownership, move semantics*

---

### ❌ Raw new/delete usage in application code

**Symptom:**
```cpp
Foo* f = new Foo(); ... delete f;
```

**Risk:** Memory leaks, double free, and ownership ambiguity

**Recommended Action:** Use RAII (std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr) for ownership. Raw pointers are only allowed as non-owning observers.


*Tags: new, delete, raii, ownership, memory leak*

---

### ❌ std::string_view pointing to temporary

**Symptom:**
```cpp
std::string_view sv = make_string();
```

**Risk:** Dangling reference after temporary object destruction

**Recommended Action:** Use std::string if ownership is needed. Verify the source object outlives the view.


*Tags: string_view, lifetime, dangling, temporary*

---

### ❌ std::span outliving underlying container

**Symptom:**
```cpp
std::span<int> get_data() { std::vector<int> v = {1,2,3}; return v; }
```

**Risk:** Dangling reference to destroyed container

**Recommended Action:** std::span is a non-owning view. Always ensure the underlying container outlives the span. Return a container by value if ownership transfer is intended.


*Tags: std::span, lifetime, dangling, view*

---


## Concurrency & Thread Safety
<a id="concurrency-thread-safety"></a>

### ❌ Assuming const implies thread safety

**Symptom:**
```cpp
All methods are const, so class is thread safe.
```

**Risk:** Data races from mutable members or referenced external state

**Recommended Action:** Explicitly verify thread safety. const only guarantees no logical modification of object state, not protection against concurrent access to shared state.


*Tags: const, thread safety, data race, concurrency*

---

### ❌ Using std::thread::detach()

**Symptom:**
```cpp
t.detach();
```

**Risk:** Threads outliving resources they reference, crash on program exit

**Recommended Action:** Use std::jthread for automatic joining, or explicitly manage thread lifecycle. Never detach threads unless you can guarantee they exit before resources they use.


*Tags: std::thread, detach, concurrency, lifetime*

---

### ❌ Mutable global variables

**Symptom:**
```cpp
int global_state = 0;
```

**Risk:** Data races, hidden side effects, impossible to reason about concurrency

**Recommended Action:** Encapsulate global state in thread-safe classes with explicit synchronization. Avoid mutable globals entirely if possible.


*Tags: global, mutable, data race, side effect*

---

### ❌ Reference capture in async lambdas

**Symptom:**
```cpp
int x = 0; std::async([&x]() { use(x); });
```

**Risk:** Dangling reference if lambda outlives the captured variable

**Recommended Action:** Use value capture (copy) for async lambdas unless you explicitly guarantee the captured variable outlives the lambda execution.


*Tags: lambda, capture, async, lifetime, dangling*

---


## Error Handling
<a id="error-handling"></a>

### ❌ Throwing exceptions from destructors

**Symptom:**
```cpp
~Foo() { if (error) throw runtime_error("failed"); }
```

**Risk:** Undefined behavior during stack unwinding if another exception is active

**Recommended Action:** Never throw from destructors. Use non-throwing error handling such as logging or std::terminate for unrecoverable errors.


*Tags: destructor, exception, undefined behavior, stack unwinding*

---

### ❌ Assuming std::expected requires exceptions

**Symptom:**
```cpp
Can't use std::expected with -fno-exceptions.
```

**Risk:** Missing out on modern error handling in no-exception environments

**Recommended Action:** std::expected works perfectly without exceptions. Use it for consistent, type-safe error handling in no-exception projects.


*Tags: std::expected, exceptions, -fno-exceptions, error handling*

---


## Performance & Optimization
<a id="performance-optimization"></a>

### ❌ Premature replacement of standard containers

**Symptom:**
```cpp
Replace std::vector with custom array for better performance.
```

**Risk:** Wasted effort introducing bugs, with minimal or no performance gain

**Recommended Action:** Always profile first to confirm the container is actually a bottleneck. Standard containers are heavily optimized and should be preferred unless there is clear, measured evidence of a problem.


*Tags: std::vector, performance, premature optimization, containers*

---


## Class & Object Model
<a id="class-object-model"></a>

### ❌ Virtual calls in constructors or destructors

**Symptom:**
```cpp
Base::Base() { virtual_method(); }
```

**Risk:** Calling base class implementation instead of derived, undefined behavior

**Recommended Action:** Never call virtual methods in constructors or destructors. The derived class isn't fully constructed yet, so virtual dispatch doesn't work as expected.


*Tags: constructor, destructor, virtual, undefined behavior*

---


## Modernization & Best Practices
<a id="modernization-best-practices"></a>

### ❌ Overly aggressive replacement of C-style arrays

**Symptom:**
```cpp
Replace all T[N] arrays with std::array<T, N> unconditionally.
```

**Risk:** Breaking API/ABI compatibility in library interfaces

**Recommended Action:** Keep C-style arrays in ABI boundaries. Modernize internally only after verifying no compatibility issues.


*Tags: array, c-style, modernization, abi*
